chunks: And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"The stingy one is not the one who pays the obligatory zakat from his wealth and gives openly among his people. Rather, the truly stingy one is he who does not pay the obligatory zakat from his wealth and does not give openly among his people, while he squanders in matters other than that."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ الْمَفْرُوضَةَ: the obligatory zakat due from one's wealth
key_terms.الْبَائِنَةَ: open and evident giving among one's people

ai.seo_question: Who is considered truly stingy in this hadith of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله؟
ai.summary: This hadith defines true miserliness not merely as withholding optional generosity, but as failing to fulfill obligatory financial duties such as zakat. It also condemns the contradiction of refusing rightful giving while wasting wealth elsewhere, linking generosity to both legal obligation and social responsibility.
